import pandas as pd

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv(DATA_PATH)

# Display the first few rows and basic information about the dataset
df_info = df.info()
df_head = df.head()

df_info, df_head

# Fill missing values with the mean
df['AverageRooms'].fillna(df['AverageRooms'].mean(), inplace=True)
df['AverageBedrooms'].fillna(df['AverageBedrooms'].mean(), inplace=True)

# Replace outlier in Income column
income_mean = df['Income'].mean()
df['Income'].replace(-999.0, income_mean, inplace=True)

# Display the cleaned dataset
cleaned_df_info = df.info()
cleaned_df_head = df.head()

cleaned_df_info, cleaned_df_head

import numpy as np

# Set the number of simulations
num_simulations = 10000

# Calculate the mean and standard deviation of the PortfolioValue
mean_portfolio_value = df['PortfolioValue'].mean()
std_portfolio_value = df['PortfolioValue'].std()

# Simulate portfolio values
simulated_returns = np.random.normal(mean_portfolio_value, std_portfolio_value, num_simulations)
simulated_portfolio_values = mean_portfolio_value + simulated_returns

# Calculate the VaR at the 95% confidence level
VaR_95 = np.percentile(simulated_portfolio_values, 5)  # 5th percentile for 95% VaR

VaR_95

# Identify losses that exceed the VaR
losses_exceeding_VaR = simulated_portfolio_values[simulated_portfolio_values < VaR_95]

# Calculate the average loss in these scenarios
average_loss_exceeding_VaR = losses_exceeding_VaR.mean()

average_loss_exceeding_VaR
